name: Lenisna

lead: Lenisna is a poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) injectable used in aesthetic clinics as a skin booster and collagen stimulator. People use PDLLA products for firmer, smoother skin.

PDLLA-HA products combine PDLLA microspheres, which stimulate collagen, with non-cross-linked hyaluronic acid as a carrier. The only source found is a 2026 expert consensus on safe injection technique for PDLLA-HA200, and efficacy studies of Lenisna were not found.

paras: A clinician injects it, and collagen-driven changes are described as building gradually after treatment.

The consensus describes a rare but serious complication: visual field impairment and blindness after accidental injection into a blood vessel, and sets out management recommendations. It is performed by trained clinicians.

angle.text: People use Lenisna as a skin booster for firmer, smoother skin. PDLLA microspheres are meant to stimulate collagen production. The main literature is a 2026 consensus on injection safety, and efficacy studies were not found.

lead: Lenisna is the name of a poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) injectable used in aesthetic medicine. The only source identified is a 2026 expert consensus on safe injection technique and the management of visual impairment caused by PDLLA-HA200, a next-generation injectable combining PDLLA microspheres with non-cross-linked hyaluronic acid as a carrier.[1]

The consensus addresses a rare but serious complication, visual field impairment and blindness, that can result from inadvertent injection into a blood vessel.[1] Efficacy studies of Lenisna were not found in the sources reviewed; the link between this consensus and the product name Lenisna is not established there beyond the PDLLA-HA200 class.

paras: No studies found. A 2026 consensus by an expert panel, not a clinical trial, sets out recommendations for safe injection technique and for managing visual impairment after PDLLA-HA injection.[1]
The consensus describes visual field impairment and blindness after inadvertent intravascular injection as rare but devastating complications of PDLLA-HA products.[1]
